children: Malaysia's benchmark Kuala Lumpur Composite Index closed 1.5% lower at 1700.54, its biggest one-day drop since March. Sentiment was weighed by U.S.-Iran strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, which caused panic selling across the board, said FSMOne research assistant manager Alwyn Chew Chuan Shyn. Despite the selloff, he expects the KLCI to remain in an uptrend. The index is expected to trade within a range as renewed Middle East tensions weigh on foreign investor sentiment, while investors also await Bank Negara Malaysia's rate decision later this week, he added. Chew pegs the KLCI's support at 1688 and resistance at 1750. Among decliners, Petronas Chemicals lost 4.2% and RHB Bank was 3.9% lower. Meanwhile, Hong Leong Bank was 0.9% higher and Hong Leong Financial Group rose 0.5%. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
